fact_check.claim: Transfers who have not met the requirement elsewhere must live on campus for one academic year
fact_check.note: Source: all new transfer students who have not fulfilled the requirement at a previous institution must live on campus one academic year.

fact_check.claim: Spring transfers live on campus the spring semester plus the following academic year
fact_check.note: Transfer page says exactly this.

fact_check.claim: Living on campus comes with a required meal plan
fact_check.note: Students in residence halls must enroll in a university meal plan.

fact_check.claim: Two exemptions: two years on campus at previous school, or matriculating as junior/senior
fact_check.note: Both listed on the transfer page. The application page mentions only the previous-institution one and refers to a Residential Policy.

fact_check.claim: You request the exemption inside the housing application itself
fact_check.note: The application page lists no exemptions and says nothing about requesting one in the application. No source link in the article for this.

fact_check.claim: 2026-27 new student application opens at 12:00 noon on April 1
fact_check.note: Page gives April 1 but no time for new students; the noon opening time listed there applies to graduate and professional students.

fact_check.claim: Cornell asks transfers to apply within ten days of receiving the NetID; described as 'the deadline' with 'cut-offs'
fact_check.note: Source says transfer students 'should also apply for housing within ten days of receiving your NetID': advice, not a stated hard deadline. Article calls it a deadline/window/cut-off, and says applying inside it keeps you off the waitlist; the source does not say that.

fact_check.claim: Timeline figure plots 2026-05-15 for the ten-day application, 2026-08-01 for the timeslot deadline and 2026-08-18 for move-in
fact_check.note: Move-in page shows only Fall 2025 (August 1, 2025 timeslot deadline; Aug 18-19, 2025) and says 2026 is not posted. 2026 dates in the figure are invented, and no source gives May 15 at all.

fact_check.claim: Confirmations begin in mid-June: a building and room, or a spot on the guaranteed waitlist with weekly updates
fact_check.note: Mid-June, guaranteed waitlist, weekly emails, rolling over summer.

fact_check.claim: Fall 2025 timeslot deadline August 1; new students moved in August 18 and 19
fact_check.note: Matches; 2026 not posted, as the article says.

fact_check.claim: Transfers may be placed in West Campus House System, South Campus halls, North Campus residence halls, and Program Houses (presented as Cornell's words)
fact_check.note: Page lists South Campus, West Campus Houses, Program Houses and (upper-level only) co-ops; North Campus is not mentioned. The linked text is not a quote from the page.

fact_check.claim: Transfer rooms are grouped together whenever possible
fact_check.note: 'whenever possible'.

fact_check.claim: A small number of transfers who qualify as first-years go into first-year housing
fact_check.note: 'In limited situations'.

fact_check.claim: West Campus is the five houses (Alice Cook, Carl Becker, Flora Rose, Hans Bethe, William Keeton) plus the Townhouse Apartments; each house has its own dining room
fact_check.note: Five houses ok. Page lists Townhouse Apartments with South Campus, not West. Dining room claim has no source.

fact_check.claim: South Campus: Cascadilla, Schuyler, Sheldon Court, 112 Edgemoor, 104 Mary Ann Wood Drive, 109 McGraw Place; closest to Collegetown, farthest from the Ag quad
fact_check.note: Building list ok. Proximity/food/nightlife/Ag quad statements have no source.

fact_check.claim: Program Houses are themed halls open to first-years and upper-level students, including Risley (arts), Holland International Living Center, Loving House
fact_check.note: Descriptions match. Page does not say each house is open to first-years; the transfer page describes Program Houses as for first-year and upper-level students. Equity & Engagement is upper-level only, so 'open to all' needs care.

fact_check.claim: Join a Program House by listing it as a preference and acknowledging its mission
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: More than 500 first-year and transfer students live in Program Houses each year
fact_check.note: 'over 500 first-year and transfer students will live in Program Houses'.

fact_check.claim: College Confidential 2025 thread: transfers placed after current students; most land in West; many to Cascadilla and Schuyler
fact_check.note: Reported by individual posters (one says placed after current students, one says most in West, one says many in Cascadilla/Schuyler 'this year'); one poster disputed the 'last' assumption. Article attributes to the thread generally, not to posters.

fact_check.claim: Posters stress West is not guaranteed; one described a suite with four other transfers
fact_check.note: No poster mentions a suite with four other transfers: invented anecdote. 'West not guaranteed' was not found either.

fact_check.claim: Cornell Daily Sun 2016: some transfers temporarily housed in North Campus lounges
fact_check.note: Jameson and High Rise 5 lounges converted to temporary housing for 30 transfers.

fact_check.claim: Cornell Daily Sun 2018: transfers had no housing guarantee and some learned their assignment in June
fact_check.note: Article says Cornell does not guarantee transfer housing; notified June 22.

fact_check.claim: Since then the residential requirement made on-campus housing mandatory for new transfers
fact_check.note: No source link; the transfer page says the requirement applies to students arriving fall 2022 or later. Causal 'since then' framing is unsourced.

fact_check.claim: Rates same in fall and spring; gas, electricity, garbage, internet up to 200 GB/month included
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Rates are per person
fact_check.note: Page does not say 'per person' in the extract.

fact_check.claim: Triple or one-room quad $6,322/semester, $12,644/year
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Double $6,872/semester, $13,744/year
fact_check.note: Matches. Note: the page prices a quad at $6,872 too; the table omits quad.

fact_check.claim: Single or townhouse double $7,783/semester, $15,566/year
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Super single $8,298/semester, $16,595/year
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Eight co-ops, among the least expensive options, most singles and doubles, four with meal plans, all shared kitchens, selection starts early February
fact_check.note: Matches. Selection starts early February, most rolling.

fact_check.claim: Co-op rates vary by house and are not on the central rate page, so you ask each house
fact_check.note: The rates page does list co-op semester rates: singles $3,949 to $5,693, doubles $3,487 to $4,981.

fact_check.claim: Co-ops are a cheap option 'most transfers never hear about' for transfers
fact_check.note: Transfer page labels co-ops 'upper-level students only'. The 'never hear about' claim is unsourced. Article does not tell first-year/sophomore transfers whether they are eligible.

fact_check.claim: Housing Office phone 607-255-5368
fact_check.note: Co-op page cites the Housing Office number; Program Houses page gives 607-255-5368 and housing@cornell.edu.

fact_check.claim: Can request single, double, triple or quad; Cornell will do its best but does not promise; lifestyle questionnaire or name a roommate; not guaranteed
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Apply the day your NetID works and list several room types; a blank second choice is read as flexibility; most new students arrive without a roommate
fact_check.note: No source states any of this; it is invented advice presented as how Cornell reads applications.

fact_check.claim: New transfers cannot cancel a housing assignment
fact_check.note: Correct, with exceptions (no longer attending, approved exemption; second-years with approved Greek/co-op).

fact_check.claim: Cancellation fees $50 through Jan 31 rising to $2,000 July 1 to Aug 15 apply to returning juniors and seniors
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: No-show by first day of classes without late arrival: assignment cancelled, billed half of fall room rate
fact_check.note: 50% of the fall semester room rate.

fact_check.claim: International transfers should email Housing before move-in; expect to arrive later; tell Housing flight date in writing
fact_check.note: Late-arrival arrangement is mentioned, but the email and 'in writing' instruction has no source.

fact_check.claim: Junior/senior transfers can still apply for on-campus housing but are placed after current students
fact_check.note: No source for this; no link.

fact_check.claim: Program Houses turn over more mid-year than West houses
fact_check.note: Unsourced factual claim.

fact_check.claim: Ranking only West Campus: a blank list hands the choice to the office; nobody reminds you about the ten-day window
fact_check.note: Unsourced assertions about how assignment works.

fact_check.claim: FAQ: Cornell's pages guarantee housing for first-years; transfer page does not use the word guarantee; apply inside the window to stay off the waitlist
fact_check.note: First two parts ok ('All first-year students are guaranteed'; transfer page has no guarantee). The waitlist cause is unsourced.

fact_check.claim: Cornell runs room-change processes during the year; internal links /housing/ and /money/
fact_check.note: No official source for room changes; the internal pages may not exist.

beats_top.why: The first Cornell University result is the official application page (the very first listing is Cornell College in Iowa). The official pages split rules, rates, timeline and placement across five pages. Our page combines them with a rate table, a timeline and attributed student experience, once its errors are fixed.
changes: Remove invented or unsourced items (noon opening time, 2026 timeline dates, suite anecdote, North Campus placement, roommate tips, Townhouse under West) so every number and date can be trusted.
Correct the co-op section: rates are on the rates page and the transfer page says co-ops are upper-level only; say who is eligible.
Say plainly that the ten-day window is Cornell's advice, not a hard deadline, and keep the first paragraph with the double rate and a 'what to do now' line.

fixes: In 'The timeline' step 1, delete 'at 12:00 noon'. The source (https://scl.cornell.edu/residential-life/housing/housing-details/apply-housing-campus) gives April 1 with no time for new students; noon applies to graduate/professional students. Also change the timeline figure row label to 'New student housing application opens' with no time.

In the timeline figure, remove the rows dated 2026-05-15, 2026-08-01 and 2026-08-18, or relabel them as the 2025 dates (2025-08-01 timeslot deadline, 2025-08-18 move-in, source https://scl.cornell.edu/residential-life/housing/housing-details/moving-campus/move-schedule). Do not plot 2026 dates the sources do not give. Replace the ten-day row with a relative label with no calendar date.

Change every description of the ten-day rule from 'deadline', 'window' and 'cut-off' to Cornell's advice: 'Transfer students should also apply for housing within ten days of receiving your NetID' (https://scl.cornell.edu/residential-life/housing/housing-details/apply-housing/new-undergrad-application-process). Delete the claims that applying inside it keeps you off the waitlist (FAQ) and that 'nobody reminds you' (Common mistakes). Fix the meta and intro to match.

Replace the paraphrase of Cornell's placement list. The transfer page (https://scl.cornell.edu/residential-life/housing/campus-housing/new-transfer-undergraduates) lists South Campus halls, the West Campus House System and Program Houses (co-ops are upper-level only); it does not mention North Campus. Remove 'North Campus residence halls' from the Cornell paraphrase, and move the Townhouse Apartments out of the West Campus bullet (the page lists them with South Campus).
Delete 'Each house has its own dining room' and 'Closest to Collegetown food and nightlife, farthest from the Ag quad', or add an official Cornell source link for each.

Delete the sentence 'One described being placed in a suite with four other transfers, which matches Cornell's grouping policy'; no poster in the linked thread says it. Also delete 'Posters there also stress that West is not guaranteed' unless a quoted-or-paraphrased poster can be linked. Keep attributing to individual posters ('one poster says most transfers land in West').

In 'What it costs', delete 'Rates vary by house and are not on the central rate page, so you ask each house.' Replace with the co-op semester rates from https://scl.cornell.edu/residential-life/housing/housing-details/rates-amenities-licenses/housing-rates: singles $3,949 to $5,693 and doubles $3,487 to $4,981 per semester (the page does not say whether fall and spring differ). Delete 'the one most transfers never hear about' and add that the transfer page lists co-ops as 'upper-level students only', so say which transfers are eligible. Add the quad ($6,872 per semester) to the rate table or the double row (label 'Double or quad').

In 'Roommates and room type', delete 'Most new students arrive without a pre-arranged roommate' and the whole paragraph beginning 'If you are hoping for a single' (apply the day your NetID works; blank second choice read as flexibility). They have no source. Replace with only what the application page says: you can request a room type and Cornell will do its best.

Delete 'You request the exemption inside the housing application itself' (no source), and instead say to contact the Housing Office at 607-255-5368 or housing@cornell.edu to ask how to document an exemption (source https://scl.cornell.edu/residential-life/housing/campus-housing/new-transfer-undergraduates/program-houses for the number).

In 'The history matters too', delete 'Since then the residential requirement has made on-campus housing mandatory for new transfers' or replace with a sourced fact: the requirement applies to students arriving fall 2022 or later (https://scl.cornell.edu/residential-life/housing/campus-housing/new-transfer-undergraduates).

In 'If you are...' delete 'but you are placed after current students, so start an off-campus search in parallel' and 'Ask about mid-year openings in Program Houses, which turn over more than the houses on West'; neither is sourced. Reword the international bullet to drop 'expect to arrive later than domestic students' and 'in writing', and link the late-arrival wording to the cancellation policy page.

In the FAQ 'Can I switch rooms after I arrive?', delete the claim that Cornell runs room-change processes and the links to /housing/ and /money/ unless those pages exist and an official room-change source is linked. Same for the '(see our housing guides)' link in the exemptions paragraph.

In the first paragraph and 'What it costs', delete 'per person' unless the rates page is quoted; also delete the claim that Program Houses are 'open to' first-years generally and instead write 'for first-year and upper-level students', noting that the Equity & Engagement community is upper-level only (https://scl.cornell.edu/residential-life/housing/campus-housing/new-transfer-undergraduates).
